limitations: Dirty source-built images have no OCI revision label; timing is exploratory and not a hosted-main baseline.
Bun/controller and observer-contract changes create separate comparison cohorts.
Failed trials retain their correct-data evidence and cannot serve as valid references.
Public refresh clients refetch raw events; the primary client also refetches task results.
Slow-client delay paces iterator consumption; SDK/socket buffers may continue reading.
Protocol clients share the generator process; this is not multiple rendered browsers.
Public freshness includes the 5-second refresh cadence and authorized typed reads.
Unprefixed LIVE latency metrics observe the private native database, not the public API. Native LIVE completeness is diagnostic; public refresh and exact persisted oracles determine correctness.
Fixed 100ms query pacing is a background reader, not a query capacity measurement.

Private raw-event drain polls at 50ms after publication, independently of public refresh. Goodput divides validated events by publication-to-durable-count time. Drain polling yields a timing upper bound and excludes public refresh.
On delivery failure, latency distributions describe successful partial observations only; they cannot establish tail latency.
Generator and observer share this process, including readiness, workload, validation and cleanup.
RSS/cgroup peaks are cumulative since startup; not publication-only or additive app memory.
Publisher lag detects unsustainable arrivals; resource averages alone do not prove headroom.
